ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl:
Fix integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n. Then r >= 0 and n-r >= 0, so both quantities [n choose r]_q and [n choose n-r]_q are defined by the given formula

[n choose s]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_s (q;q)_{n-s})

for the relevant values s=r and s=n-r.

Now compute directly from the definition:

[n choose n-r]_q
= (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_{n-r} (q;q)_{n-(n-r)})
= (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_{n-r} (q;q)_r).

Since multiplication is commutative,

(q;q)_{n-r} (q;q)_r = (q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}.

Therefore

[n choose n-r]_q
= (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r})
= [n choose r]_q.

So the two defining expressions are identical. Hence the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient is symmetric under replacing r by n-r; in particular, [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q as polynomials in q.

payload.statement_nl: For all integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, define the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient by [n choose r]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}), where (q;q)_m := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^i) and (q;q)_0 := 1. Then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q as polynomials in q.

dependency_assessment.notes: Proof uses only the lemma's own stated definition and basic algebraic commutativity.

detailed_findings.finding: Direct computation from the defining formula establishes the symmetry identity exactly.

result_payload.reason: The proof is a complete direct verification from the stated definition of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Under 0 <= r <= n, both r and n-r are nonnegative, so both defining expressions are legitimate. Substituting s = n-r into the formula gives [n choose n-r]_q = (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_{n-r}(q;q)_r), and commutativity of multiplication identifies this denominator with ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}), which is exactly the denominator for [n choose r]_q. Hence the two expressions are identical as polynomials in q. There is no reliance on the root theorem or other forbidden dependencies.
